# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 101 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 101 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_101_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 18

**1** "Now I understand, Lord," I said, "but I want to ask further whether those who have repented can still be placed into the tower." **2** "They can," he said, "if they repent and put away the works of these women, and if the names of the good virgins are given back to them so that they themselves bear those names." **3** "And when," I asked, "will those stones that were thrown aside be fitted in?" **4** "When they repent," he said. **5** "But if they do not repent quickly, they will not enter the tower; entry is possible only while the tower is still being built." **6** "And will it be possible for them to repent, Lord?" **7** "It is possible; but if the tower is completed before they repent, they will no longer have a place in the building — for there will be no more room." **8** "Lord," I said, "I wish to ask something further." "Ask," he said. **9** "Will the repentant have a place in the tower if they repent, even if they were great sinners?" **10** "Yes," he said, "if they truly repent and put away the works of wickedness, they can be built into the tower. But not in the prominent places — they shall be placed in lower and inferior positions. However they shall be built in if they repent now, before the tower is completed." **11** "And if any repent after the tower is complete?" "They shall be excluded from the tower. Only the Lord knows whether any such repentant sinners can enter the kingdom of God." **12** "But since we have been told this from you now, Lord, we will repent with all our heart before the tower is finished." He smiled and said, "You are rightly glad about this, and you have spoken the truth."

---

### Translator's Note
This chapter contains the Shepherd's most nuanced statement about post-baptismal repentance: it is effective but not unlimited, and late repentance brings entry at a lower position rather than full equivalence. The completion of the tower as the eschatological deadline is hammered repeatedly. The Shepherd's laugh in v. 12 is one of the warmest moments in the entire text. SOPHIA follows LOGOS throughout.
